subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: Should OpenClaw accept this experimental core `claws remove` contract—especially retention of referenced global plugins, selected cleanup overrides, and no permanent removal tombstone—as the supported lifecycle direction for the stacked Claws feature?
rationale: The patch can implement either policy safely, but choosing the long-lived ownership, recovery, and operator-audit contract is a maintainer product decision rather than a mechanical code correction.

options.title: Approve the lifecycle contract after proof
options.body: Accept the documented retain-by-default, explicit cleanup, and no-tombstone policy once final-head terminal evidence covers the conflict and cleanup branches.

options.title: Require a retained audit record
options.body: Ask for a narrow lifecycle record or recovery surface before accepting deletion of completed active provenance rows.

options.title: Keep the slice out of core
options.body: Defer the experimental lifecycle surface until the RFC direction and stacked feature ownership are settled.

recommendation.title: Approve the lifecycle contract after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the documented retain-by-default, explicit cleanup, and no-tombstone policy once final-head terminal evidence covers the conflict and cleanup branches.

likelyOwner.reason: Their RFC feedback directly addresses the ownership rule that determines removal behavior.
